To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cross lingual transfer in XLM R is more pronounced in simpler downstream tasks.

(i) cross lingual transfer in XLM R is strongest in STS, (ii) the degree of cross linguistic transfer is softened as the complexity of the task increases, (iii) the degree of the cross lingual transfer varies across languages, and (iv) the degree of transfer can be measured by the performance of a downstream task on a zero shot setting.
(1) the cross lingual transfer ability is most pronounced in semantic textual similarity (2) it is the next in sentiment analysis (3) and it is the last in machine reading comprehension.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: 1) How does XLM R transfer in various NLP tasks?; 2) How much transfer does it bring in each task?; 3) How does the complexity of a task affect the transfer?; 4) How can we measure the transfer empirically?; and, 5) Can we make use of transfer in a practical way?
the following: 1. How much cross lingual transfer does a supervised NLP model trained on a source corpus in a source language exhibit?
the following questions: (1) How strong is cross lingual transfer in supervised NLP? (2) What are its limitations? (3) How can we improve cross lingual transfer?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XLM R is not a silver bullet for zero shot cross ling ling transfer in supervised NLP tasks.
the cross lingual transfer in supervised NLP tasks is possible and effective, but it is not as strong as it might be expected.
the degree of crosslingual transfer is proportional to the complexity of the downstream task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XLM R is a strong cross lingual language representation model that is particularly effective for STS and sentiment analysis.
cross lingual transfer in XLM R is more pronounced than in other models and the degree of transfer depends on the task complexity.
the cross lingual transfer induced by XLM R is most prominent in the simplest task, STS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross lingual transfer induced by XLM R is a powerful tool to be used in downstream NLP tasks.
the cross lingual transfer of XLM R is not universal, and the extent of transfer depends on the task and the language pair.
XLM R pretraining is not a panacea for cross lingual transfer but a useful step towards the goal.
